content: Base phrase chunking is a cheap sequence-labeling–based alternative to full syntactic parsing, where the sequence consists of non-overlapping labeled segments (Fig. FIGREF1 includes an example.) Full syntactic trees can be converted into such shallow syntactic chunk sequences using a deterministic procedure BIBREF9. BIBREF12 offered a rule-based transformation deriving non-overlapping chunks from phrase-structure trees as found in the Penn Treebank BIBREF13. The procedure percolates some syntactic phrase nodes from a phrase-syntactic tree to the phrase in the leaves of the tree. All overlapping embedded phrases are then removed, and the remainder of the phrase gets the percolated label—this usually corresponds to the head word of the phrase.
